😞 7.4 million families went without the basics. In October, the bills go up again.

The Joseph Rowntree Foundation's summer tracker found 62% of low-income families — around 7.4 MILLION — couldn't afford at least one essential in six months. Adequate food. Heating. Shoes that fit their children. It's a record, and it's up from 7.1 million a year ago.

⚡ Now look at 1 October: Ofgem's price cap rises 4%, from £1,663 to £1,723. That's £60 a year on a typical bill. Gas bills alone up 8%.

✅ Credit where it's due — scrapping VAT on electricity is worth about £45.
❌ But £45 off against £60 on still leaves you going backwards. That's not help. It's a smaller loss with a bigger press release.

And the Prime Minister nobody elected won't rule out tax rises in the autumn.
